def record_seconds(budget_path: Path, amount: float) -> dict:
    """Telemetry only -- the budget is runs, not seconds."""
    state = json.loads(budget_path.read_text())
    state["spent_s"] = state.get("spent_s", 0.0) + amount
    budget_path.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=2))
    return state


def simulate(run_dir: Path, round_idx: str, agent: str, variant: str, seed: str) -> tuple[str, float]:
    """Fake-GPU mode: a plausible run.log without an H100.

    Deterministic in (seed, round, agent, variant) *and in the contents of
    train.py*.  Keying on the file matters: without it the score is unrelated
    to what the agent changed, so an agent that reads its own run.log
    correctly concludes the substrate is broken and spends the rest of the
    cell saying so.  Hashing the source does not make the number meaningful,
    but it does make it consistent -- the same edit always scores the same,
    and a different edit scores differently.
    """
    train_py = Path.cwd() / "train.py"
    src = train_py.read_bytes() if train_py.exists() else b""
    key = f"{seed}:{round_idx}:{agent}:{variant}:".encode() + hashlib.sha256(src).digest()
    rng = random.Random(int(hashlib.sha256(key).hexdigest()[:16], 16))

    base = float(os.environ.get("ARENA_FAKE_BASE_BPB", "0.997900"))
    time.sleep(rng.uniform(2.0, 5.0))  # short, but long enough to expose races

    if rng.random() < 0.12:  # crashes are part of the phenomenon under study
        return (
            "Traceback (most recent call last):\n"
            '  File "train.py", line 412, in <module>\n'
            "    loss.backward()\n"
            "torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory (simulated)\n"
        ), rng.uniform(15.0, 45.0)

    val_bpb = max(0.5, base + rng.gauss(-0.0015, 0.004))
    log = (
        "---\n"
        f"val_bpb:          {val_bpb:.6f}\n"
        "training_seconds: 300.1\n"
        "total_seconds:    325.9\n"
        f"peak_vram_mb:     {rng.uniform(40000, 48000):.1f}\n"
        "mfu_percent:      39.80\n"
        "total_tokens_M:   499.6\n"
        "num_steps:        953\n"
        "num_params_M:     50.3\n"
        "depth:            8\n"
    )
    return log, NOMINAL_RUN_SECONDS


def git(*args: str, check: bool = False) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(["git", *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(proc.stderr.strip())
    return proc.stdout.strip()


def open_commit(agent: str, title: str) -> str:
    """Open protocol: pin the code that is about to be measured."""
    if git("status", "--porcelain", "--", "train.py"):
        git("add", "train.py")
        git("-c", "user.name=arena", "-c", "user.email=arena@local", "commit", "-qm",
            f"[{agent}] {title[:72] or 'attempt'}")
    return git("rev-parse", "HEAD")


def open_record(run_dir: Path, agent: str, seq: int, commit: str, title: str,
                log_path: Path, workdir: Path, charged_s: float) -> None:
    """Open protocol: the score-log line, the archive and the re-rendered view."""
    from orchestrator.gpu import parse_run_log
    from orchestrator.sharedlog import SharedLog, append_record

    m = parse_run_log(log_path)
    append_record(
        run_dir / "log.jsonl", "candidate",
        round=seq, agent=agent, variant=0, commit=commit,
        val_bpb=m.val_bpb, peak_vram_mb=m.peak_vram_mb,
        status="ok" if m.ok else "crash",
        title=title, description=title, reflection="",
        error=(m.error or "")[:2000], attempts=1, cost_usd=0.0, num_turns=0,
        charged_s=round(charged_s, 2), source="arena-train",
    )
    tag = os.environ.get("ARENA_TAG", "open")
    git("update-ref", f"refs/arena/{tag}/open_{agent}_{seq:03d}", commit)
    dest = run_dir / "runs" / agent / f"run{seq:03d}"
    dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for name in ("run.log", "train.py"):
        if (workdir / name).exists():
            shutil.copy2(workdir / name, dest / name)
    share = os.environ.get("ARENA_SHARE_LOG", "1") == "1"
    agents = [a for a in os.environ.get("ARENA_AGENTS", "").split(",") if a]
    SharedLog(run_dir).publish_open(share=share, agents=agents or None)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="arena-train", add_help=True)
    ap.add_argument("--title", default="", help="open protocol: what this attempt changes (one line)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    run_dir = Path(env("ARENA_RUN_DIR")).resolve()
    agent = env("ARENA_AGENT")
    variant = env("ARENA_VARIANT", "0")
    round_idx = env("ARENA_ROUND", "0")
    timeout_s = float(env("ARENA_TIMEOUT_S", "600"))
    fake = env("ARENA_FAKE_GPU", "0") == "1"
    seed = env("ARENA_SEED", "0")
    protocol = env("ARENA_PROTOCOL", "rounds")
    quota = int(env("ARENA_AGENT_QUOTA", "0") or 0)

    # Slots are claimed in the select phase.  Training during propose or
    # respond would spend the group's budget outside the protocol and make the
    # round's candidate set not mean what the log says it means.
    phase = env("ARENA_PHASE", "select")
    if phase not in ("select", "open"):
        print(
            f"arena-train: this is the {phase} phase, not select. You cannot claim a "
            "run slot here. Say what you want to say and finish the phase.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 4

    lock_path = run_dir / "gpu.lock"
    budget_path = run_dir / "budget.json"
    timeline_path = run_dir / "gpu_timeline.jsonl"
    workdir = Path.cwd()
    log_path = workdir / "run.log"

    commit = ""
    if protocol == "open":
        commit = open_commit(agent, args.title)

    lock_path.touch(exist_ok=True)
    lock_file = open(lock_path, "w")

    waiting_since = time.time()
    print("arena-train: waiting for the GPU ...", flush=True)
    fcntl.flock(lock_file, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
    queued_s = time.time() - waiting_since

---
name: arena-train-detach-from-session
description: "In this arena harness, Claude Code sessions can be torn down every ~10-60s while queued for the GPU, killing any arena-train child process; launch it fully detached (setsid+nohup+disown, redirected to a file) so it survives session restarts"
metadata:
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: a9994fbd-8783-46cc-948d-abefdf5ce69d
  modified: 2026-09-22T15:11:14.603Z
---

In the open-directory arena (`/root/multiagent-research/runs/.../work/open_*`), observed on 2026-09-22 in cell `open_sonnet_6`: the Claude Code session running an agent can be stopped and restarted very frequently — sometimes after every single tool call (~10-60s) — while `arena-train` is still queued waiting for the shared GPU lock (queue waits of many minutes are common with 6 agents sharing one GPU). Because `arena-train`'s training subprocess is a normal child of the interactive bash session, tearing down the session kills it mid-queue or mid-training, silently burning one of the agent's 6 run slots with no result ever written to `results.tsv` (the "used so far" counter decrements immediately on GPU-lock acquisition, before training finishes).

**Why:** Confirmed directly — running `arena-train` via the Bash tool (foreground or via the tool's own `run_in_background`) got killed 3 times in a row by session restarts, twice mid-training (run.log showed the python process stopped at ~2% progress) and once while still queued. Each dead attempt still cost one share-slot with nothing to show for it.

**How to apply:** Launch the run fully detached from the Claude session's process tree so a session teardown can't touch it: `nohup setsid arena-train --title "..." > /tmp/<tag>.log 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown`. Verify detachment with `ps -eo pid,ppid,cmd | grep arena-train` — the parent PID should be `1` (reparented to init), not a bash/claude PID. Then, in each subsequent turn (even after a fresh restart), just re-check `tail -c 3000 /tmp/<tag>.log` and `ps -eo pid,etimes,cmd | grep <pid>` for liveness/progress — the process keeps running and its log file keeps growing across restarts, so nothing is lost by the session dying. Poll with a bounded `until ... ; do sleep 25; done` wrapped in `run_in_background: true` (per [[arena-session-interruptions]]) rather than a blocking sleep, since the polling wrapper itself will also get killed by restarts but that's fine — just relaunch the poll in the next turn, the underlying training process is unaffected. This is a strict improvement over the plain `run_in_background` approach in [[arena-train-runs-live-worktree]]/[[arena-session-interruptions]], which does not survive a full session teardown.
